name: FragBASIC
_comment: Word lists are the 61 reserved words in Lexer.KEYWORDS (src/fragbasic_core/lexer.py) plus the 35 builtin functions the interpreter dispatches, split by role so every reserved word lands in exactly one category. All matching is case-insensitive: the lexer compares word.upper() against KEYWORDS, so `print`, `Print` and `PRINT` are the same token.

comment_apostrophe.comment: An apostrophe opens a comment ONLY at the start of a line (ignoring indentation) -- Lexer.is_at_start_of_line(). Anywhere else it opens a QB64 single-quoted string, handled by #string_single. Matched from column 0 so it beats a later double quote on the same line.

comment_rem.comment: REM consumes the rest of the line wherever it appears.
comment_rem.name: comment.line.rem.fragbasic

string_double.comment: No escape sequences -- the lexer runs from one quote to the next, so a double-quoted string cannot contain a double quote. Ended at end-of-line too, so an unterminated string does not colour the rest of the file.
string_double.name: string.quoted.double.fragbasic

string_single.comment: QB64 single-quoted string -- only reachable mid-line, since a leading apostrophe was already taken as a comment.
string_single.name: string.quoted.single.fragbasic

line_number.comment: A classic BASIC line number: digits at the very start of a line.
line_number.name: constant.numeric.line-number.fragbasic

keyword_declaration.comment: Type names and declaration modifiers. STRING is here rather than with the builtins; STRING$ (the padding function) is a separate word and lives in #support_builtin.
keyword_declaration.name: storage.type.fragbasic

support_builtin.comment: The 35 functions the interpreter dispatches by name. The $-suffixed ones are listed before any bare prefix could win, and the whole rule sits before #variable_typed so LEFT$ is a builtin rather than a string variable named LEFT.
support_builtin.name: support.function.builtin.fragbasic

constant_numeric.comment: A number, optionally with a QBasic type suffix (% integer, & long, ! single, # double).
constant_numeric.name: constant.numeric.fragbasic

variable_typed.comment: An identifier carrying a QBasic type sigil -- name$ is a string, name% an integer, and so on. Plain identifiers are left unscoped, as they are in every other language here.
variable_typed.name: variable.other.fragbasic

patterns.comment: <> before < and >; <= and >= before the bare forms.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.comparison.fragbasic

patterns.comment: `=` is both assignment and equality in BASIC.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.assignment.fragbasic

patterns.comment: `;` separates PRINT items; `:` separates statements on one line.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.fragbasic
